newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Kuchma security aide says Ukraine could join NATO.
newsitem.headline: Kuchma security aide says Ukraine could join NATO.

text.p: President Leonid Kuchma's closest aide said on Wednesday it was possible Ukraine could join NATO in the future -- another sign the former Soviet republic was moving closer to the Western alliance which was once its enemy.

"I do not exclude the possibility that the time will come when Ukraine will become a NATO member. The potential possibility of this really exists," Security and Defence Council Secretary Volodymyr Horbulin told reporters.

Ukraine wants membership of the European Union and associate membership of the Western European Union defence grouping. But it has so far ruled out joining NATO for now, saying it just wanted to move closer to the alliance.
Hurbulin's remarks indicated Kiev might be moving towards a more active pursuit of NATO membership.
The prospect of Ukrainian NATO membership would certainly alarm Russia which, together with Belarus, has resisted the prospect of eastern European countries joining NATO.
Moscow fears it would end up isolated if the alliance extended right up to their borders.
Hurbulin, also a personal friend of the president, made clear in comments after a briefing that closer ties between Ukraine and NATO could eventually lead to full membership.
"We have already established such relations with NATO that allow us to talk about a rapprochement to the point where we would become, possibly, some kind of NATO member," he said.
Hurbulin praised NATO as a security structure, mentioning its role in ending the conflict in former Yugoslavia.
"The Yugoslavia events have shown this structure has really worked effectively. The ethnic and religious war there would never have stopped (without NATO)," he said.
Ukraine is one of the most active participants in NATO's "Partnership for Peace" programme. It has hosted several military exercises with NATO troops.

Kiev's only objection to expansion of the Western alliance eastwards was its fear that NATO nuclear arms could end up in Central and Eastern Europe. But the alliance has since said it has no plans for such a deployment.
